question:
(a) Explain the formation of an $n$-type semiconductor by doping silicon with a pentavalent impurity.
(b) Identify the majority and minority charge carriers in it. Why is its conductivity higher than that of a pure semiconductor?

options.A:
(a) n-type silicon is formed by a trivalent impurity, which creates a hole.
(b) Holes are majority carriers and conductivity decreases.
options.B:
(a) Doping silicon with a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus or arsenic lets four impurity electrons form covalent bonds while the fifth is weakly bound and easily becomes free, giving n-type semiconductor.
(b) Electrons are majority carriers and holes are minority carriers. The added free electrons greatly increase mobile carrier concentration, so conductivity is higher than in pure silicon.
options.C:
(a) n-type material is formed without dopant by cooling silicon to absolute zero.
(b) Both electrons and holes vanish, so conductivity increases.
options.D:
(a) A pentavalent impurity accepts electrons from silicon and creates only holes.
(b) Holes are majority carriers and conductivity remains unchanged.
